title: Side Effects of Microdosing Lysergic Acid Diethylamide and Psilocybin: A Systematic Review of Potential Physiological and Psychiatric Outcomes | Microdosing Institute
abstract:
- The side effects of microdosing LSD and psilocybin are mostly mild, dose-dependent, and transient, including increased blood pressure, anxiety, and cognitive impairment.
- There’s a significant lack of standardized reporting on side effects across studies, which hampers the ability to draw clear conclusions about the safety of microdosing practices.
- Future research should prioritize systematic methodologies, longer study durations, and standardized assessments to accurately evaluate the risks and benefits of microdosing.
### Physiological Side Effects  
Gastrointestinal issues, especially nausea and stomach discomfort, were prevalent in studies revolving around psilocybin microdosing. Some users reported mild digestive issues, which generally subsided quickly. In LSD studies, headaches surfaced frequently after the primary effects diminished, while psilocybin microdosing seemed to result in fewer instances of headaches.  
Notably, microdosing psychedelics was associated with slight, temporary spikes in blood pressure, particularly at higher doses, with values returning to normal within a few hours. These increases were more pronounced in individuals administering doses of 20 micrograms of LSD or higher. Fluctuations in body temperature were also mentioned, although lab studies did not identify significant physiological changes.
